nodes.title: Comparison determinant line
nodes.statement: For a genuine motive M/Q with coefficient number field E, a selected embedding into C and supplied finite free Betti and de Rham realizations B,D of equal rank d, let β:D⊗C ≃ B⊗C be the integration comparison and I=β⁻¹. Define the comparison period as the nonzero element det(I) of Hom(det B,det D)⊗C. In column coordinates P=[I], replacing Betti basis b by bA and de Rham basis d by dC gives P′=C⁻¹PA and det P′=det(C)⁻¹det(P)det(A). No existence of geometric realizations is asserted from arbitrary linear algebra.

nodes.title: Tate and elliptic normalization examples
nodes.statement: Choose the counterclockwise loop on Gm and the form dz/z. Integration on Q(−1)=H¹(Gm) is 2πi, so Deligne’s I has δ(Q(n))=(2πi)^n, F∞=(−1)^n and type (−n,−n). For an elliptic curve E/R with oriented integral cycles γ₁,γ₂ and an algebraic de Rham basis ω,η, write the integration matrix B=(∫γᵢωⱼ)_{i,j}; the column-coordinate comparison is β=Bᵗ and I=(Bᵗ)⁻¹. The all-components real Néron period is the number of components times the positive identity-component integral. Relating it to a primitive B⁺ cycle requires the integral index at 2, not only a rational eigenspace. In the concrete curve y²=x(1−x)(1−x/2), take ω=dx/(2y), η=xω. Let γ_a traverse [0,1] with y positive and return on the opposite sheet, and γ_b traverse [1,2] with y=−i√(x(x−1)(1−x/2)) and return on the other sheet. Put K=∫₀¹dt/√((1−t²)(1−t²/2)), J=∫₀¹t²dt/√((1−t²)(1−t²/2)), H=∫₁²x dx/(2√(x(x−1)(1−x/2))). Then the row-cycle integration matrix is B=[[2K,2J],[2iK,2iH]], with the positive-imaginary γ_b orientation and the complementary-modulus identity at 1/2. Its column comparison is (Bᵗ)⁻¹; equivalently if a=2K,b=2J,c=2iK,d=2iH, it is (ad−bc)⁻¹[[d,−c],[−b,a]]. No numerical approximation is used to assert this equality.
hypotheses: Elliptic uniformization, minimal invariant differential and actual integration supplied by the existing EllipticCurves and ComplexComparison roadmaps.
The basis matrix is nonsingular; orientation and form/cycle order fixed.
proofSteps: Evaluate dz/z on the chosen loop and invert the comparison.
Use the already constructed Tate Hodge type; supply the geometric comparison scalar separately.
Form the elliptic matrix with rows cycles and columns forms, then transpose before inverting.
Import the all-components real-period convention and keep its lattice index visible.

nodes.title: Motivic Euler product
nodes.statement: A weakly compatible system R consists of a number field E⊂C, a finite bad set S, monic degree-d polynomials Q_v over E for v∉S, continuous semisimple representations over algebraic closures of E_λ r_λ unramified away from Sλ with those Frobenius characteristic polynomials, de Rham local restrictions at v|λ (crystalline outside S), and multisets H_τ for τ:F→Ebar agreeing with the labelled Hodge–Tate weights under every embedding Ebar→Ebar_λ over E. Strict compatibility additionally supplies, at every finite v, a WD representation over an algebraic closure of E whose scalar extension under every coefficient embedding equals WD(r_λ|G_v)^{F-ss}, including v|λ. Purity of weight w is the existing monodromy-filtration purity of each supplied WD representation; no descent of r_λ to E_λ is implicit. For this admitted system with Hodge/infinity realizations, import P_v(T)=det(1−T Fr_geom | (ker N_v)^{I_v}) and L_v=P_v(q_v^(−s))⁻¹. Define L_fin by its absolutely convergent Euler product for Re(s)>1+w/2; the proof bounds the local reciprocal roots by q_v^(w/2) and compares the resulting prime sum with the trivial-character Hecke Euler product. L_fin^S omits S. Retain every bad-place WD factor. Use local conductor exponents with an explicitly supplied global base-field/discriminant normalization N(R). Continuation is separate analytic data.
hypotheses: Strict compatibility includes the Frobenius-semisimplified WD comparison for every coefficient place, including v above its residue characteristic.
The imported monodromy-filtration purity bounds the eigenvalues on ker N by q_v^(w/2); Hodge and infinity data are additional inputs when not supplied by geometry.
proofSteps: Import the actual continuous Galois representations, local WD construction and conductor exponents from AGR; formulate the BCGP compatible-system predicate here. AGR R01.5 recognition is not a construction of compatible systems.
Apply determinant polynomials on inertia-invariant monodromy kernels; prove coefficient-embedding independence using strict compatibility.

For Re(s)>1+w/2, bound the local reciprocal roots and compare the absolute logarithmic series with the supplier’s trivial-character Hecke Euler product. Keep full and partial products and their finite ratio distinct.

nodes.statement: Specialize imported rational interval arithmetic and certified subdivision to actual period integrals. On [0,1], D_λ≥1−λ and |f′_λ|≤8/(1−λ)^(3/2). Thus N≥1 midpoint panels have error ≤2/[N(1−λ)^(3/2)]. Replace this real bound by any certified larger rational and enclose every square root by positive rational square inequalities, adding the accumulated arithmetic widths. For y²=x(1−x)(1−λx), ω=dx/(2y), the oriented real oval over [0,1] has period 2K_λ. This is a specified cycle period; an all-components Néron period requires the separate elliptic adapter.
